deck: 192 PRACTITIONERS TEST BUY-LOW, SELL-HIGH FLIPS AGAINST NAMEBIO COMPS, AI APPRAISALS, AND RENEWAL MATH
THEY BUILD PORTFOLIOS FROM EXPIRED-DOMAIN HUNTS, DEDICATED REGISTRARS, MARKETPLACE LISTINGS, OUTBOUND SALES, AND ESCROW-CLOSED DEALS
site_ui.lead: Domain Investing distills 192 practitioners on how to source cheap names, vet them against comparable sales, list them across Afternic, Sedo, and Atom, and close safely through escrow without letting renewal fees eat the margin.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies, spanning beginner flips, registrar and DNS setup, expired-domain auctions, valuation, negotiation, parking, trademarks, and capital. Every claim carries timestamped inline attribution to the channel and video it came from, so each tactic, price point, and warning traces back to its source.

Registrars and DNS Infrastructure for the Domain Portfolio
Hunting Expired Domains: Auctions, Backorders, and Drop Catching

Marketplace Listings: Afternic, Sedo, and Atom
Closing the Deal: Escrow, Lease-to-Own, and Seller Safety
Trademarks, Disputes, and the TLD Landscape
flow: Hand-register or snipe cheap names via ExpiredDomains.net, auctions, backorders, and drop catching, treating AI-generated name lists as raw ore
Reject dashes, misspellings, numbers, and dates; favor short, memorable .com first with .ai and .io as alternates, and audit backlinks and Wayback history on aged names
Pair GoDaddy appraisals with NameBio comparable sales, discount highball AI estimates, and cap beginner buys around $20 to $50 per name
Hold names at a dedicated registrar with free WHOIS privacy priced on renewal rate, and point nameservers to Afternic to cut commission from 25% to 15%
List wide on Afternic, Sedo, Atom, and Namecheap, pitch niche businesses directly, and relist at a new price after 90 days unsold
Refuse pay-later buyers and close through escrow or lease-to-own before transfer, then auto-renew keepers and drop dead weight before the renewal bill hits

tagline: Big Money. Small Teams. No Bullshit.
